cards.headline: The Strokes fired Radiohead's producer mid-album
cards.snippet: In 2003, straight after touring their debut Is This It, the Strokes went back into the studio for their second album, Room on Fire. They hired Nigel Godrich, who had produced Radiohead, but fired him because, in the band's words, their work together was "soulless". Godrich said he and singer Julian Casablancas were both control freaks. Those sessions were scrapped, and the band returned to their first producer, Gordon Raphael. They had exactly three months of studio time left. "What Ever Happened?" opens the album that came out of that rushed second attempt.
cards.context: The opener 'What Ever Happened?' comes from the rushed second attempt at the album.

cards.headline: Rolling Stone heard a broken speakerphone in a burning building
cards.snippet: In its review of the Strokes' second album, Room on Fire, published in October 2003, Rolling Stone singled out the opening track, "What Ever Happened?". It said Julian Casablancas' voice is so distorted by fuzz in the first verse that he sounds like he is singing over a broken speakerphone from a burning building. The review described a band that had changed since its cocky debut two years earlier. It heard more distance and distrust than on Is This It, even though the album's sound was otherwise much like the first.
cards.context: Review of the album's opening track, published October 2003.

cards.headline: A shout to Tennessee Williams, then a line that sticks in the head
cards.snippet: The line points to Tennessee Williams, who wrote "A Streetcar Named Desire." Stanley drunkenly screams Stella's name, a scene made famous by Marlon Brando. Julian can't do that, because he expects his girl to let him down.
cards.context: Fans belt it back in the comments: "OH TENNESSEE WHAT DID YOU WRITEEEEEEEEEEE"
